seo.title: Kitchen sink
seo.description: Every part of the default theme in the context of a page: the edge cases a real site runs into sooner or later.

values.heading: Kitchen sink
values.body:
The pages under this one show the default theme at its edges: long words, dark blocks in the main column, blocks side by side on a narrow screen.
They come with the demo and go with php artisan webx:demo --remove — a real site never has them.

seo.title: Long words
seo.description: Words longer than a phone is wide, in the languages that have them.

values.heading: Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaftskapitänsmützenabzeichen
values.body: German glues nouns together: Rindfleischetikettierungsüberwachungsaufgabenübertragungsgesetz was a real law, and a heading like the one above has to break inside the word rather than push the page sideways.

values.heading: Konstantynopolitańczykowianeczka
values.body: Polish brings its own letters and its own lengths: najprawdopodobniej, dziewięćdziesięciokilkuletni, współpracowniczka. Ąą Ćć Ęę Łł Ńń Óó Śś Źź Żż — every one of them in the font the theme names.

values.heading: Превысокомногорассмотрительствующий
values.body:
Cyrillic, which a site with Russian among its languages prints on every page: человеконенавистничество, высокопревосходительство.
An address with no place to break: https://example.com/a/very/long/path/that/goes/on/and/on/without/a/single/space/in/it/anywhere

seo.title: Blocks in the column
seo.description: A dark block, text and columns one after another in the main column of the page.

values.title: A dark block in the main column
values.subtitle: The prose of the theme reaches every block inside the page, so its colours must not assume a light background: this heading and this line stay readable on navy.

values.heading: Text right after it
values.body: The column and the blocks share one left edge, and nothing on this page scrolls sideways at 360 pixels.

values.heading: One
values.body: Three columns on a wide screen, one under another on a phone.

values.heading: Two
values.body: A column with a longer text in it, so that the three are not the same height and the grid has to say what it does about that.

values.heading: Three
values.body: Short.

seo.title: Header and menu
seo.description: The header of the theme at every width: dropdowns, the mobile menu, a sticky bar and anchors under it.

values.heading: The header and the mobile menu
values.body:
Every page has the header of the theme, so this one is about trying it. Hover the items with an arrow: a dropdown opens after a short delay and stays while the pointer goes to it. On a phone the first tap opens it and the second follows the link. From the keyboard Enter or Space opens a dropdown, the arrows move inside, Esc closes it.
Make the window narrower: the items fold into the menu exactly when they no longer fit in a row, not at a fixed width.

values.heading: The mobile menu
values.body: It opens from the right with the logo on top and the call to action at the bottom. The page under it does not scroll; its own body does. Back in the browser closes it instead of leaving the page, and so does a swipe to the right. A branch of the menu opens over its parent, with Back and the branch name on top; the branch of the page you are on is open already.

values.heading: A sticky header and anchors
values.body: The header stays on top while the page scrolls. A link to a heading further down stops below the header rather than under it: the header keeps its height in --webx-header-height and the page scrolls by it.

values.heading: A long page to scroll
values.body:
This text is here so that the page is longer than a phone. Scroll down and up again and watch the header stay.
Lorem ipsum is not used on purpose: a showcase in words reads as a page, and a page is what the header lives on.
The next pages go two levels deeper, which is where the mobile menu needs Back.

seo.title: Second level
seo.description: A page one level below the header showcase, with a page under it in turn.

values.heading: Second level
values.body: In the header this page is an entry of the dropdown under Kitchen sink › Header and menu. In the mobile menu it is a branch of its own.

seo.title: Third level
seo.description: Three levels down: the mobile menu opens on this branch with Back to each level above.

values.heading: Third level
values.body: Open the mobile menu here: it starts on this branch, the page marked as current, and Back goes up one level at a time.

seo.title: Cookie consent
seo.description: The cookie banner of the widgets: rejecting, customising, taking an answer back and Global Privacy Control.

values.heading: The cookie banner
values.body:
Every page asks until the visitor answers: a short text, a link to the policy and three buttons. Reject all and Accept all are the same size and the same weight, because consent won with a big green button next to a grey link is no consent. On a phone the banner never covers more than a third of the screen; a long text scrolls inside it and the buttons stay.
The answer is the cookie webx_consent: the categories, the date and the version of the policy. When the policy changes, the panel raises the version and everyone is asked again.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
Reject all: the banner goes and nothing third-party loads on any page. Reload — it does not come back.
Customize: a dialog with a switch per category. Necessary is always on; a category nothing on the site uses is not offered at all, so a site without a counter does not ask about statistics.
Cookie settings in the footer opens the same dialog on any page. Switch off something you agreed to and the page reloads: a script that already ran cannot be unloaded.
To start again, delete the webx_consent cookie in the developer tools.

values.heading: Global Privacy Control
values.body: A browser that sends Sec-GPC (Brave, or Firefox with the setting on) asks sites not to track it. Here that means marketing is never part of Accept all and the dialog says why; the visitor can still switch it on by hand.

values.heading: For the site
values.body:
Anything third-party waits for its category: a script written as type="text/plain" with data-webx-consent="statistics", an iframe with data-webx-consent="media" and data-src instead of src, or any code inside <x-webx-consent category="marketing">. Once agreed to, the script runs, the iframe loads, the code goes on the page.
Scripts of the site ask webx.consent.has('media') and listen to webx:consent. Google Consent Mode v2 is on by itself: denied by default in the head, updated after the answer.

children.title: Dropdown and form in a dialog

seo.title: Dropdown and form in a dialog
seo.description: A form of the inbox opened in a dialog from any button, and the dropdown panel the phones and the languages are built on.

values.title: A form in a dialog
values.subtitle: The button below is a link to #webx-form-contact. On a page with that link the site prints the Contact us form once, in a dialog at the end of the page, and the button opens it.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
Open the form on a phone: the dialog fits the screen, a long form scrolls inside it while the title and the close button stay on top, and the page under it does not move. Tab goes round the dialog and never reaches the page; Esc closes it and gives the focus back to the button.
Send the form: the dialog shows the thank-you of the form and a Close button, and waits — it never closes by itself. In the panel the submission says it came from the place modal.
Two buttons on this page open the same form, and the page has it once. With JavaScript off the button is a link that shows the same dialog over the page.

values.heading: For the site
values.body: Any link or button opens a form of the inbox by its slug: data-webx-form="callback", or simply href="#webx-form-callback" — the second one can be typed into a menu item or the button of a block in the panel. data-webx-form-value-service="12" fills the hidden field service of the form, so Book from a service page arrives with the service. An opener the server never prints asks for its form with Widgets::form('callback').

values.heading: The dropdown panel
values.body:
x-webx-dropdown is a panel tied to its trigger: the phones, the opening hours and the language switcher of the next stages are built on it. Without JavaScript it is a details element that opens under its trigger. With it the panel lifts above everything around it, turns over at the edge of the window, opens on hover when asked, closes on Esc, on Tab out and on a click elsewhere, and only one is open on the page.
The starter run (pnpm test:starter) puts a row of them on this page and measures that.

values.title: Still have a question?
values.subtitle: A second button to the same form: the page still has one.

seo.title: Contacts
seo.description: Phone numbers, opening hours, chats and networks from the Contacts tab of the settings, in the header, the footer and the corner of the window.

values.title: Contacts typed once
values.subtitle: Everything on this page that rings, writes or says when the office is open comes from one place: Settings › Contacts in the panel. Change a number there and the header, the footer, the button in the corner and the markup for search engines change with it.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
Above the header: the opening hours — "Open until 7:00 PM" or "Closed, opens tomorrow at 9:00 AM", in the time zone of the office in London, not yours. Open it: the week in a table, Monday to Friday folded into one row, today in bold. Leave the page open past seven: the status changes by itself.
In the header: the main number, a link that dials it, its WhatsApp and Telegram beside it, and the arrow — the other numbers with their labels. On a phone the numbers are at the bottom of the menu.
In the corner: the round button opens the chats, the number and the e-mail. While the cookie banner is on the screen the button stands above it.
In the footer: every number, the e-mail, the address that opens a map, and the networks as icons.

values.heading: In the panel
values.body:
Settings › Contacts: the numbers with their labels and messengers, the e-mails, the addresses with their coordinates, the hours as rows of days, the special dates that replace a weekday, the time zone, the chats and the networks.
A number has to start with + and its country code: "020 7946 0958" is refused with a word on what to add, because the site cannot tell which country it is in — a language is not a country. The page shows the number as it was typed; the link dials it in E.164, +442079460958.
The same keys are settings over MCP: an agent asked to change the phone on the site changes it in one place.

values.heading: For the site
values.body:
x-webx-phones (layout="list", compact, callback="<form>"), x-webx-hours (layout="table"), x-webx-contact-button (corner, form, :items), x-webx-contact-bar (form, :breakpoint) and x-webx-socials read the Contacts tab and print nothing while it is empty. In a template: contacts()->primaryPhone(), contacts()->hours()->openNow(), contacts()->addresses().
The organisation in the markup of every page takes its telephone, e-mail and address from the same tab, and becomes a LocalBusiness with its place and opening hours once they are filled in.

seo.title: Language switcher
seo.description: The same page in the site’s other languages, from the address registry — the home page of a language where the page is not translated yet.

values.title: One page, every language
values.subtitle: The globe in the header lists the languages of the site, each in its own words: English, Русский, Polski. A link leads to this very page in that language — or, while it has no translation, to that language’s home page, and says so.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
Open the globe in the header: the current language is marked, the other two are greyed — this page is in English only, so they lead to the Russian and the Polish home pages. Hover one: its title says so in that language.
Go to the home page and open the globe there: the home page is in all three languages, and every link leads to it — the same page, nothing greyed.
On a phone the switcher is at the bottom of the menu, with the numbers. With the keyboard: Enter opens it, Tab walks the languages, Esc closes it and gives the focus back to the globe.
A site in one language has no switcher at all: there is nothing to switch to.

values.heading: Where the addresses come from
values.body:
From the address registry — the same rows hreflang in the head of the page is built from. A page, an article, a product has its address in each language it is translated into; the switcher leads there. A module’s own address, such as the blog’s list, is the same path under the other language’s prefix.
A translation that is hidden in a language is no translation: the link leads home. So does a page that does not exist.
The switcher needs the language in the address (/pl/…). With the language read from the browser instead, every language has one address and there is nothing for a link to choose.

values.heading: For the site
values.body:
x-webx-language-switcher — the dropdown, or layout="list" for the languages in a row; codes adds EN, RU, PL; placement for the dropdown; label and fallback-label replace the words. Classes: webx-language-switcher, __current, __list, __link, is-current, is-fallback. No flags: a flag is a country, not a language.
In a template: WebxUi\Widgets\Languages\LanguageLinks::current() — the same links, to draw them your own way.

seo.title: Slider
seo.description: The slider in every variant, at full width and in a narrow column.

values.heading: Slider
values.body:
Four variants of one widget: cards, hero, gallery and logos. Slides per view follow the width of the column the slider stands in, not the width of the window — so the same cards show three to a row here and one and a bit in the narrow column below.
The gallery and the logos are the blocks of the same names — what a site puts on a page in the panel, with pictures of the media library. The rest stand on a block made for this page.
Without JavaScript every slider is a strip that scrolls sideways and stops at a slide.

values.heading: Cards
values.note: Three per view at full width, two on a tablet, one and a bit on a phone. The arrows move a whole view; the dots are pages.

values.heading: Cards in a narrow column
values.note: The same cards in a column 20rem wide: one and a bit per view, whatever the width of the window.

values.heading: Hero
values.note: One slide to the width, fading, turning on its own every six seconds. It stops while the pointer or the focus is inside, and the first button stops it for good; with reduced motion it does not start.

values.heading: Gallery in a narrow column
values.note: The thumbnails scroll when they do not fit.

values.heading: One slide
values.note: Nothing to move: no arrows, no dots.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
Narrow the window: the full-width cards go from three to two to one and a bit; the narrow ones stay as they are.
With the keyboard: Tab into a slider, then the arrows, Home and End move it — only the slider the focus is in. A link in a slide that is out of view brings its slide in when it gets the focus.
On a phone: swipe. The page still scrolls up and down over a slider.
Switch JavaScript off: every slider is a strip that scrolls sideways and snaps to a slide, the arrows and dots are gone, and so are the thumbnails.

values.heading: For the site
values.body:
x-webx-slider with x-webx-slide inside. variant — cards, hero, gallery, logos; per-view — a number, or by the width of the slider: ['sm' => 1.2, 'md' => 2, 'lg' => 3] (sm from 0, md from 640px, lg from 960px, xl from 1280px, or a width in pixels); arrows, pagination, loop, autoplay (milliseconds, true or false), effect (slide or fade), thumbs, speed, label; options — anything else Swiper takes. A slide's thumb names the picture of its thumbnail.
Classes: webx-slider, webx-slider--<variant>, __viewport, __track, __slide, __controls, __button, __prev, __next, __pause, __pagination, __bullet, __thumbs, __thumb; is-ready, is-active. Tokens: --webx-slider-gap, --webx-slider-arrow-size, --webx-slider-per-view and the rest of --webx-slider-*.
In the panel: the block gallery (pictures of the library, view grid or slider, zoom) and the block logos (a name, a logo and a link each) — offered by webx-ui/widgets, installed by webx:blocks:offered --install --module=widgets.

seo.title: Lightbox
seo.description: Pictures that open over the page: the gallery block as a grid and as a slider, links written by hand.

values.heading: Lightbox
values.body:
A picture that opens over the page, at the size of the screen, and pages through the pictures of its group. It is a link to the picture: without JavaScript the link simply opens it.
The grid and the slider are the gallery block with pictures of the media library: one group per block, the sizes stored at upload, a title of a picture printed under it. The page loads the lightbox only because a link on it asks for one — data-webx-lightbox, wherever it was written.

pictures.title: Photo 1 — a caption from the library
Photo 2 — a caption from the library
Photo 3 — a caption from the library
Photo 4 — a caption from the library
Photo 5 — a caption from the library
Photo 6 — a caption from the library

values.heading: Links by hand
values.note: Two links written in a template with no component, each on its own. The first is taller than wide — on a phone it fits by its height. The second came without its sizes: it is measured before it opens.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
With the keyboard: Tab to a picture and press Enter; the arrows page, Esc closes, and the focus is back on the picture you ended on.
On a phone: swipe to the next picture, pinch to zoom, swipe down to close.
Switch JavaScript off: every picture is a link that opens the file.

values.heading: For the site
values.body:
x-webx-lightbox :image="$picture" group="product-1" — image is a value of a media field (url, thumb, alt, width, height) or any object with url() and width and height; src, width, height, thumb, alt say it by hand. The slot replaces the thumbnail.
By hand: a href="picture" data-webx-lightbox="group" data-width="2400" data-height="1600" — the same group pages together, an empty one is alone. Write the sizes: without them the picture is loaded once more to be measured.
Classes: webx-lightbox-link, __image, is-ready; the viewer is PhotoSwipe's .pswp with webx-lightbox on it. Tokens: --webx-lightbox-backdrop, --webx-lightbox-color, --webx-lightbox-outline, --webx-lightbox-placeholder, --webx-lightbox-icon-size, --webx-lightbox-z.

seo.title: Video
seo.description: The Video block: YouTube and Vimeo as a facade, the placeholder before consent, a file of the site, posters, captions and shapes.

values.heading: Video
values.body:
Every video on this page is the Video block of the widgets but one — a column 20rem wide, which a block cannot stand in. A YouTube or Vimeo video is a facade: a poster and a play button, and the player only on a click. Until a visitor agrees to media, the server prints a placeholder in its place — the poster, a line saying where the video loads from, Load and Always load videos — and nothing on this page asks YouTube or Vimeo for anything, the posters included: they are pictures of the site.
A video of the site is a video element that loads nothing before Play, with no consent to ask for: it is first party. The line under each video is the block’s caption.

values.heading: YouTube, a poster from the library
values.caption: The poster is a picture of the media library, picked for the video.

values.heading: YouTube, no poster
values.caption: No poster picked: the site fetched the video’s preview once into its library (folder Video posters). The first page that showed it had none.

values.heading: Vimeo, no poster
values.caption: The same with Vimeo, whose preview its oEmbed names.

values.heading: A video of the site
values.caption: A file of the media library with a poster: nothing loads before Play, and there is nothing to agree to.

values.heading: A video of the site, no poster
values.caption: Without a poster the frame keeps its place until Play.

values.note: The placeholder keeps the ratio in a column 20rem wide, its buttons inside the frame.
values.heading: In a narrow column
A ratio of its own
values.caption: Shape 4:3 — the frame has its height before anything loads.

values.heading: Upright
values.caption: Shape 9:16, as a phone films: held to a phone’s width in the middle of the column.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
Before an answer, or after Reject all: every YouTube and Vimeo video is the placeholder. Load plays that one and agrees to nothing; Always load videos agrees to media — the banner is answered, every placeholder becomes a play button without a reload, the one you clicked plays.
After consent: the play button puts the player in, with the focus in it. Take media back in Cookie settings in the footer: the page reloads with the placeholders.
With the keyboard: Tab reaches each play button, Enter plays.
Switch JavaScript off: each video is a link to its page with its poster; a file of the site still plays.

values.heading: For the site
values.body:
The Video block: a heading, a link or a file (a switch says which), a poster, a caption and a shape — 16:9, 4:3, 1:1 or 9:16. An address of no known provider, a file gone from the library or nothing at all prints nothing.
x-webx-video src="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=…" :poster="$picture" title="…" — an address of YouTube (watch, youtu.be, shorts, embed, live) or Vimeo (unlisted with its hash too); a start from ?t= or #t= is kept.
x-webx-video :file="$media" :poster="$picture" ratio="4:3" — a value of a media field, an object with url() or an address; ratio is 16/9 unless told.
Classes: webx-video, --youtube, --vimeo, --file, __facade, __poster, __play, __consent, __notice, __button, __frame, __player; is-blocked, is-ready, is-playing. Tokens: --webx-video-ratio, --webx-video-bg, --webx-video-radius, --webx-video-play-size, --webx-video-play-bg, --webx-video-play-color, --webx-video-notice-bg, --webx-video-button-bg.

seo.title: Map
seo.description: The Map block: OpenStreetMap through Leaflet, the address of the contacts or coordinates of its own, the placeholder before consent, the wheel that scrolls the page.

values.heading: Map
values.body:
Every map on this page is the Map block of the widgets but one — a column 20rem wide, which a block cannot stand in. The map is Leaflet over the tiles of OpenStreetMap, which need no key. Tiles are requests to another site with the visitor’s address, so until a visitor agrees to media the server prints the place instead — the address, Open in maps, a line saying where the map loads from, Load and Always load maps — and nothing on this page asks OpenStreetMap for anything.
The attribution of the map’s data stands in the corner of every map, before it loads and after: its licence asks for it.

The map above has no coordinates of its own: it reads the main address of the Contacts tab of the settings — its text, latitude and longitude, its link to a map. Change the address there and every map from the contacts moves with it.

values.heading: In a narrow column
values.note: The placeholder keeps the map’s height in a column 20rem wide, its buttons inside the frame.

values.heading: What to try
values.body:
Before an answer, or after Reject all: every map is its place. Load puts that one map in and agrees to nothing; Always load maps agrees to media — the banner is answered and every map on the page loads without a reload.
Over a loaded map the wheel scrolls the page and says how to zoom; click the map, and the wheel zooms it; press anywhere else, or leave it with the mouse, and the wheel scrolls the page again. On a phone one finger scrolls the page until the map is tapped. With the keyboard: Tab reaches the map, the arrows pan it, + and − zoom.
Take media back in Cookie settings in the footer: the page reloads with the places.
Switch JavaScript off: each map is its address and a link to a map.

values.heading: For the site
values.body:
The Map block: a heading, the place — from the contacts or coordinates with an address of their own — a zoom from 1 to 19 and a height: low, medium or tall. Nowhere to show — no address in the contacts, no coordinates — prints nothing.
x-webx-map from="settings" — the main address of the Contacts tab; an address without coordinates is the place alone, with no map.
x-webx-map :lat="51.5074" :lng="-0.1278" :zoom="15" marker="1 Example Street, London" height="24rem" — marker is the pin’s label (false: no pin), height a CSS length or a number of pixels, link the address of Open in maps.
The provider of the tiles is config: webx-widgets.map.provider — openstreetmap, or maptiler with WEBX_MAP_KEY, or an entry of your own with the address of a tile.
Classes: webx-map, --place, __place, __address, __open, __notice, __button, __attribution, __canvas, __marker, __hint; is-blocked, is-ready, is-loaded, is-active. Tokens: --webx-map-height, --webx-map-bg, --webx-map-radius, --webx-map-marker, --webx-map-notice-bg, --webx-map-button-bg, --webx-map-attribution-bg, --webx-map-hint-bg.
